ownership_reason: Only the gold visits the elements of the range one by one; hop 1 packs the three values, hop 2 takes the whole array as the range, hops 3 and 4 pass the range along. Once the running lowest value has been seeded with 0 instead of the first element of the range, the lowest of an all-positive range is lost (the result is 0 whatever the values), so no hop can recover it and no one-line change of the packed values or the range bounds makes the start value harmless for every input. The convention that the result is one of the values, seeded from the first one, is pinned outside the gold: the sibling overload NumberUtils.minimum(int, int, int) starts from its first argument (testMinimumInt); math.NumberUtils.min(long[]) seeds with array[0] and math.NumberUtils.min(long, long, long) starts from a (math NumberUtilsTest testMinLong expects min({5}) = 5 and min({6, 9}) = 6; testMinimumLong expects 12345).
